  html:

  echo: false
  warning: false
---

This brief analysis summarizes a small sample of 2026 election results across a set of states. The goal is to compare vote totals by party and state, and to see which states are the closest contests.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)

results <- read_csv("data/election_results.csv")
```

## Total votes by party

```{r party-summary}
party_totals <- results |>
  group_by(party) |>
  summarise(votes = sum(votes), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(votes))

party_totals
```

```{r party-bar-chart}
party_totals |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(party, votes), y = votes, fill = party)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Total votes by party",
    x = "Party",
    y = "Votes cast"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## State-by-state comparison

```{r state-summary}
state_summary <- results |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(
    total_votes = sum(votes),
    democratic_votes = sum(votes[party == "Democratic"]),
    republican_votes = sum(votes[party == "Republican"]),
    margin = democratic_votes - republican_votes,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_votes))

state_summary
```

```{r state-plot}
state_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(state, total_votes), y = total_votes)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Total votes by state",
    x = "State",
    y = "Total votes"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Closest races

The closest races are the ones with the smallest margins between the Democratic and Republican candidates.

```{r closest-races}
closest_races <- results |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(
    democratic_votes = sum(votes[party == "Democratic"]),
    republican_votes = sum(votes[party == "Republican"]),
    margin = abs(democratic_votes - republican_votes),
    winner = if_else(democratic_votes > republican_votes, "Democratic", "Republican"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(margin)

closest_races
```

In this sample, the tightest contest is the one with the smallest margin between major-party candidates. These close contests are often the most informative for understanding turnout and vote-share patterns heading into election night.
